Incorporating the Federal Reserve’s Financial Stability Report (FSR), the hawkish December 14, 2022 FOMC action (raising the target range to 4.25–4.50% and signaling ongoing increases, alongside higher IORB at 4.4% and ON RRP at 4.3% and continued QT) lands against an already fragile market backdrop. The FSR highlights strained Treasury market liquidity and elevated rate volatility, rising term premiums and yields, and vulnerabilities in nonbank financial intermediaries and money market funds that could amplify shocks. It also notes cooling housing (Case‑Shiller/CoreLogic/Zillow data) and pockets of leverage/credit risk (e.g., leveraged finance, CRE), plus stress in digital assets. While banks’ capital and liquidity are solid, implying resilience, the FSR suggests tighter policy will transmit forcefully through financial conditions, increasing downside risks to growth and risk assets relative to a neutral baseline. Net: slightly more negative than a pure policy‑only read.
